{{Family name hatnote|[[Wang (surname)|Wang]]|lang=Chinese}}
'''Wang Shouguan''' ({{zh|s=王绶琯}}; 15 January 1923 – 28 January 2021) was a Chinese astronomer, president and honorary president of the {{ill|Chinese Astronomical Society|zh|中国天文学会}}.<ref name="koko">{{cite news|author1=Yu Hanqi ({{lang|zh|虞涵棋}})|author2=Wang Xinxin ({{lang|zh|王心馨}})|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_10994996 |script-title=zh:中国射电天文奠基人王绶琯院士逝世，享年98岁 |trans-title=Academician Wang Shouguan, founder of radio astronomy in China, dies at the age of 98|work=thepaper.cn |date=29 January 2021 |access-date=30 January 2021 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="Las">{{cite news|author1=Sun Zifa ({{lang|zh|孙自法}})|url=https://new.qq.com/rain/a/20210129A0CADR00 |script-title=zh:中国射电天文学开创者王绶琯院士逝世 享年98岁 |trans-title=Academician Wang Shouguan, founder of radio astronomy in China, dies at the age of 98|work=qq.com |date=29 January 2021 |access-date=30 January 2021 |language=zh}}</ref> He was hailed as one of the founders of modern astrophysics and radio astronomy in China.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> He was a delegate to the [[5th National People's Congress|5th]], [[6th National People's Congress|6th]], [[7th National People's Congress|7th]] and [[8th National People's Congress]].<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/>

==Biography==
Wang was born in [[Fuzhou]], [[Fujian]], on January 15, 1923.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> His uncle worked in the [[Republic of China Navy]].<ref name="tang">{{cite news|url=https://new.qq.com/omn/20210129/20210129A0DEB500.html |script-title=zh:巨星陨落！王绶琯院士逝世，他是“能听懂星星说话的人” |trans-title=Star fall! Academician Wang Shouguan passed away, he was "a man who can understand stars" |work=qq.com |date=29 January 2021 |access-date=30 January 2021 |language=zh}}</ref> In 1936, at the age of 13, he entered {{ill|Mawei Naval School|zh|马尾海军学校}}, he studied [[navigation]] at the beginning, but switched to [[shipbuilding]] later because of [[Near-sightedness|myopia]].<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/><ref name="tang"/> After graduating in 1943, he worked at a factory for a year.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> In 1945, he pursued advanced studies in the [[United Kingdom]], where he studied at the Shipbuilding Class, [[Royal Naval College, Greenwich]].<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> In 1950 he switched to [[astronomy]], and was hired as an assistant astronomer at the [[University of London]].<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/>

Wang returned to China in 1953.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> He successively worked at the [[Purple Mountain Observatory]], Xujiahui Observatory, and [[Beijing Astronomical Observatory]].<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> In 1981, he became deputy director of the Department of Mathematical Physics, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]],  rising to director in 1994.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/> In October 1993, the [[asteroid]] with international code [[Meanings of minor planet names: 3001–4000|3171]] was named "Wangshouguan".<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/>

On January 28, 2021, he died of illness in [[Beijing]], aged 98.<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://k.sina.com.cn/article_2090512390_7c9ab00602001fdhm.html |script-title=zh:著名天文学家、中国科学院院士王绶琯逝世 |trans-title=Wang Shouguan, a famous astronomer and academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, is dead |work=sina |date=29 January 2021 |access-date=30 January 2021 |language=zh}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* 1980 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS)<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/>
* 1996 Science and Technology Progress Award of the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation]]
* 1998 Member of the International Eurasian Academy of Sciences<ref name="koko"/><ref name="Las"/>
